newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU laws not retroactive beyond Spanish accession - Court.
newsitem.headline: EU laws not retroactive beyond Spanish accession - Court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday protection for Spanish employees whose company has transferred ownership cannot precede the accession of Spain to the European Union.
After being laid off in 1993, employees of a Spanish textile company which changed ownership several times between 1978 and 1986 were denied redundancy payments for the period prior to 1978.
Under Spanish law, the government justified the denial on a distinction between experience and length of service.

The applicants looked to Council directive 77/187, which provides protection for workers laid off during the sale of a business, but were told by the court that the directive was not in effect for member states in 1978, and certainly not for Spain which was not yet a member of the EU.
Reference from Juzgado de lo Social No 16, Barcelona (Spain) between
Pedro Burdalo Tevejo and Others and

on the interpretation of article 1(1) and article 3(3) of Council Directive 77/187/EEC on the laws relating to safeguarding employee's rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses (OJ 1977 L 61, p. 26)

Council Directive 77/187/EEC on the laws relating to safeguarding employee's rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses cannot be relied on in relation to a transfer of an undertaking which took place before the directive had begun to produce legal effects in the member state concerned.
